## Question

How does greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from agrifood systems for the top 5 producing countries differ and change over the 20 year period from 2001 to 2021?

## Data Cleaning

The data will be cleaned to only include relevant columns, that is those that show the country, year and amount of GHG emissions for agrifood systems produced for that year. Then the column names will be re-labeled. Also any irrelevant rows will be removed, such as World and South Asia data as these are not countries and are unrelated to the research question. Furthermore, only data between the relevant 20 year period, that is 2001 to 2021 will be kept.

```{r}
### Load Packages###
 
#install.packages("tidyverse")
#install.packages("janitor")

library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(countrycode)
library(janitor)

```

```{r}
###Reading CSV File & Viewing Data###

unedited_data <-
  read_csv("../Inputs/unedited_data.csv") #Reading data from csv file store in folder

head (unedited_data) #Viewing top 6 rows
tail (unedited_data) #Viewing bottom 6 rows
```

```{r}
###Cleaning Data to Include Only Relevant Columns###
 
cleaned_data <- 
   select(unedited_data, 
         REF_AREA_LABEL, # Country name
         TIME_PERIOD, # Year
         OBS_VALUE) # Amount of GHG emissions in kilotonnes for that year

head(cleaned_data)
```

```{r}
###Relabeling Column Names in the Cleaned Data###

cleaned_data <-
cleaned_data |>
  as_tibble() |>
  clean_names() |>
  mutate(
    Country = ref_area_label,
    Year = time_period,
    GHG_Emissions_Kilotonnes = obs_value
    ) |>
  select(Country, Year, GHG_Emissions_Kilotonnes)

head(cleaned_data)
```

```{r}
### Filtering the Data to Only include Country Data###

countries <- codelist |>
  select(country.name.en)

cleaned_data <- cleaned_data |>
  filter(Country %in% countries$country.name.en)

cleaned_data
 
```

```{r}
### Filtering Data to only includes the years from 2001 to 2021###

cleaned_data <- cleaned_data |>
  filter(Year %in% 2001:2021)

cleaned_data

```

## Tests

Then, the class of each column will be checked to ensure that values are of the right class. Further tests using "validator" will be done to ensure that the data in each column adheres to certain rules. A csv file of the cleaned data will be created.

```{r}
### Load Packages###

#install.packages("validate")

library(validate)

```

```{r}
### Test to check the class of all columns###

class(cleaned_data$Country) 
class(cleaned_data$Year)
class(cleaned_data$GHG_Emissions_Kilotonnes)

```

```{r}
###Test to check if data in columns adheres to certain rules###

rules <- validator(
  is.numeric(Year), #Checking if the column is numeric
  is.character(Country), #Checking if the column a character
  is.numeric(GHG_Emissions_Kilotonnes), #Checking if the column is numeric
  Year %in% 2001:2021, # Checking if the years between 2001:2021
  Country %in% countries$country.name.en #Checking that all the countries name are accurate
)

out <-
  confront(cleaned_data, rules)
summary(out) 

```

```{r}
###Create CSV File of Cleaned Data###

write.csv(cleaned_data, "cleaned_data.csv", row.names = FALSE)

```

## Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) (NB: be sure to label graphs, eg. Fig 1 etc.)

After using popular functions to look at the data, three exploratory graphs will be created to help better understand the data. First, a line graph of the GHG Emission for all the countries. This will broadly demonstrate which countries are the top GHG emissions for agri-food systems. Once the top 5 countries are identified, a graph of the average amount GHG emissions for agrifoods systems  over the 20 year period for the top 5 producing countries will be plotted, this will illustrate which country produces the overall highest amount of GHG emissions for agrifood systems. Lastly, a bar chart showing the net difference in GHG emissions in agrifood systems for the top 5 producing countries between 2001 and 2021 will be plot. This will illustrate how much countries increased or decreased their overall GHG emissions for agrifood systems over 20 year period. 

```{r}
### Load Packages###

#install.packages("readr")
#install.packages("ggrepel")

library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
library(ggrepel)

```

```{r}
### Reading Cleaned Data from the CSV file###

cleaned_data <-
  read_csv("../Inputs/cleaned_data.csv")

cleaned_data

```

```{r}
###Using popular functions to get a look at the data###

head(cleaned_data)

tail(cleaned_data)

cleaned_data |>
  slice_sample(n = 5)

glimpse(cleaned_data) 

summary(cleaned_data)
```

```{r}
###Plotting a line graph###
    
cleaned_data |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = Year,
    y = GHG_Emissions_Kilotonnes,
    group = Country
  )) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_text(
    data = cleaned_data |>
      dplyr::group_by(Country) |>
      dplyr::filter(Year == max(Year)),
    aes(label = Country),
    size = 2,
    hjust = -0.1
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.15))
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```
```{r}
### Bar Graph of Mean Agrifood Systems GHG Emissions for Top 5 Emitting Countries Between 2001 and 2021###

top5 <- c("China", "Brazil", "India", "United States", "Indonesia")

mean_top5 <- cleaned_data |>
  filter(Country %in% top5) |>
  group_by(Country) |>
  summarise(Mean_Emissions = mean(GHG_Emissions_Kilotonnes, na.rm = TRUE))

ggplot(mean_top5, aes(x = reorder(Country, Mean_Emissions), y = Mean_Emissions, fill = Country)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Mean Agrifood Systems GHG Emissions for Top 5 Emitting Countries Between 2001 and 2021",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Mean Emissions (Kilotonnes)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() 
```


```{r}
### Bar Chart Showing the Net Difference in GHG Emissions in Agrifood Systems for the Top 5 Producing Countries between 2001 and 2021###

change_top5 <- cleaned_data |>
  filter(Country %in% top5, Year %in% c(2001, 2021)) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Year,
    values_from = GHG_Emissions_Kilotonnes,
    names_prefix = "y"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Change = y2021 - y2001,
    Direction = ifelse(Change >= 0, "Increase", "Decrease")
  )

ggplot(change_top5, aes(x = reorder(Country, Change), y = Change, fill = Direction)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Increase" = "firebrick", "Decrease" = "steelblue")) +
  labs(
    title = "Change in GHG Emissions Between 2001 and 2021",
    subtitle = "Top 5 emitting countries",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Change in Emissions (Kilotonnes)",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```


## Notes on Surprises in the Data

The first thing that surprised me was that the data had world data and some other non-country data such as data for South Asia. When graphs for EDA was done during the weekly practices the values for these categories either skewed the graph, int he case of the world data which was the total values for all the countries or made it difficult to figure out the top producing countries, int he case of South Asia which ranked relatively high but consisted of data from numerous counties in South Asia. As such only country data based on the country list was include for EDA in this assignment.

Also surprising was that once the line graph of all the countries was plotted it was very easy to identify which countries were the to 5 producers of GHG emissions for agrifood systems. They were quite apparent from the line graph and so further analysis like creating wide data from the cleaned data and calculating the average GHG emissions for agrifoods systems for each country to figure out which countries had a highest values over the 20 year period was unnecessary.
